title: docs/derived/state/removals.json — the killed-feature removal contract
description: AUTHORED by the project (path overridable via respawnpack.config.json state.removals.registry). Enforced at runtime by kernel/lib/removals.js readRegistry(). ⛔ AN EMPTY ARRAY IS CANNOT_DETERMINE, NOT A PASS: NOT_APPLICABLE must be DECLARED, never inferred from finding nothing. The one way to declare it here is `emptyBaseline` — see that property. additionalProperties is TRUE: `reason` is carried by real registries and read by humans, not by code.

schemaVersion.description: Hard-checked: a registry declaring any other version yields CANNOT_DETERMINE with the mismatch named, never a pass.

emptyBaseline.description: ⛔ A STRING THAT IS THE REASON, so it cannot be declared without justifying it. It says this project's retirement baseline is ESTABLISHED and deliberately empty — a claim someone made and can be reviewed, not an absence a scanner inferred. Without it, a configured scan over an empty registry is CANNOT_DETERMINE forever, because the only thing that clears it is a retirement the project has not made yet, and the founder's alternatives were to un-configure a scan they will need or to let a red check become furniture. Applies ONLY while `removals` is empty: the moment a row lands the rows are the contract and this is ignored, so a stale note cannot suppress a real registry. Declared blank or non-string is CANNOT_DETERMINE.

forbidden.description: The FORBIDDEN LIVE ASSERTIONS that would reintroduce the feature — not the feature's name. Naming a retirement is not making one, so a retirement sentence, a prohibition, a blockquote, a history section, fenced code and a struck line all pass.

controls.description: Overrides the synthesized probe. Every row is checked with a known-good and a known-bad control BEFORE its verdict counts; a phrase that is itself retirement vocabulary can never match and stops at `unverified`.
